session: An Investors community for alumni in tech investing
text: The owner reviewed public copy for US legal exposure before approving a new investing-related page, asking to remove anything that could read as connecting founders with investors.

session: An Investors community for alumni in tech investing
text: Joining a community is a two-step process the site had no way to express: apply to the HIT WhatsApp community, then request the specific group from inside WhatsApp.

session: Community-worded empty events, and AI spelled out
text: The site owner asked for an acronym community name (AI) to be spelled out in big headings but kept short in the menu and running text — a single 'name' field could not express both.

session: Pre-launch phone, tablet and desktop check
text: The owner rejected an 'organizing principles' row added to the homepage Our mission band as too wordy and poorly organized, and had the plan deleted — they want the homepage bands brief.

session: Pre-launch phone, tablet and desktop check
text: No one had looked at the site on an iPad since the September menu fix; the homepage scrolled sideways at 768–834px until an automated width sweep found it.

session: Fall 2026 volunteer roles on /volunteer
text: The volunteer sheet repeats each role across 'N of ∞' rows and leaves several roles with placeholder text, so publishing it took consolidation and judgment rather than a straight copy.

session: Fall 2026 volunteer roles on /volunteer
text: The owner wants sign-ups to go through the single volunteer interest form rather than per-role contacts.

session: Programs label retired on Events and Webinars
text: The owner asked whether the live site's webinars were ported; 10 of 11 already were, and the 11th was only a link to an external page that is now dead.

session: A reworked Events page with image cards
text: The owner wanted past events to look as visual as they do on Luma; every linked event already had square cover art on Luma that the site was not showing.

session: A reworked Events page with image cards
text: The owner noticed two link styles (arrow text links and pills) and asked what the rule was; a two-level rule existed in the stylesheet but was undocumented and applied unevenly.

session: Site facts refreshed from the October all-hands
text: Event cover images come from Luma and are pre-event promotional art, so a past event's card still advertised early-bird tickets after its write-up was changed to the result.

session: Site facts refreshed from the October all-hands
text: The site's public figures (events, attendees, communities) are repeated in five places — content, page copy, a JSON fallback, component defaults and fixtures — and an update means finding every copy by hand.

session: Simpler WhatsApp-only city pages
text: The owner found the long, em-dash-heavy copy on the WhatsApp-only city pages read as AI-written filler and asked for those pages to carry only three asks: join WhatsApp, the newsletter, and volunteering or co-leading.

session: Simpler WhatsApp-only city pages
text: The owner noticed the brand written several ways (Harvard in Tech, lowercase Harvard alumni in tech) and wants Harvard Alumni in Tech used everywhere, testimonial quotes included.

session: One brand name everywhere: Harvard Alumni in Tech
text: The owner asked why the webinars page showed no recordings; the empty state they saw was leftover preview test data, but nothing on screen told them the preview was showing a test scenario rather than the real site.

session: HIT Directory teaser in the WhatsApp band
text: The user rejected the first teaser and a decorated redesign as looking 'AI generated', and settled only after the card was rebuilt from the site's own existing card pattern.

session: HIT Directory teaser in the WhatsApp band
text: The user decided between layouts by seeing four real variants side by side, then combined two of them, rather than describing the layout up front.

session: Content-gap list and go-public hold on the cutover runbook
text: The team has no single place that says what content is still missing before launch; the owner's 'nothing ships empty' rule could only be checked by visiting every page.

session: Content-gap list and go-public hold on the cutover runbook
text: The queued plans for this project were one-line placeholders created from deferred deliverables, so each had to be re-scoped from scratch at the plan gate.

session: The site, polished for phones and tablets
text: On a 390px phone the homepage's 38-photo event wall ran to about 2,500px of scrolling between the support band and Contact; a visitor had to swipe through it to reach the contact details.

session: The site, polished for phones and tablets
text: Volunteer roles without a photo showed an empty pink placeholder band on phones, so a visitor scrolled through about 18 blank boxes to read the open roles.

session: Retired brand names flagged in the content admin
text: The owner wanted retired brand wording caught while volunteers edit in the content admin, not only by a developer test; the editor surface had no way for a site to declare its own wording rules.

session: CMS uploads publish freely; Nicole's photos and lead headshots placed
text: Images Nicole uploaded through the content admin blocked every deploy until a developer hand-wrote credit and alt-text records for each file.

session: CMS uploads publish freely; Nicole's photos and lead headshots placed
text: Nicole uploaded event photos while trying to fill the London gallery, but nothing recorded which chapter they were for, so placement had to be inferred and confirmed with her afterwards.
